description:
- From butterfly guard, establish a 2-on-1 grip on their arm by grabbing their wrist with one hand and their tricep/elbow with the other
- Use your butterfly hook on the same side to elevate and off-balance them toward the trapped arm
- As they post or react, duck under their trapped arm and circle to their back
- Secure one hook in first, then work to establish the second hook and seatbelt grip
- Keep your chest tight to their back to prevent them from turning into you

- From closed guard bottom, secure an underhook on one side and grab their opposite wrist (arm drag setup)
- Pull their arm across your body while simultaneously opening your guard and pivoting on your shoulder
- Use your legs to help guide their body over you as you circle toward their back
- As they pass over, immediately work to establish your first hook behind their thigh
- Secure the seatbelt grip and work to get your second hook in for full back control

- From knee on belly position, reach across and secure an arm drag grip on their far arm
- Pull their arm across while stepping your knee-on-belly leg over to the opposite side
- Circle around their head toward their back, keeping the arm drag control
- As you move behind them, immediately work to establish your first hook
- Secure seatbelt grip and work to get both hooks in for back control

- From 411/saddle position, control their far leg and maintain your inside position
- When they turn away to defend the leg attacks, follow their movement
- Climb up their back by walking your hands up their torso
- Establish your first hook as they continue turning away from the leg entanglement
- Secure seatbelt grip and work to establish the second hook for full back control

- From bottom half guard, work to establish deep half guard by getting your bottom arm deep under their far leg
- Use your underhook to lift and roll them over you toward the trapped leg side
- As they roll over, immediately start working toward their back by following the roll
- Establish your first hook as you come up behind them
- Secure seatbelt control and work to get both hooks in for back control

- From leg drag position (controlling their legs to one side), maintain control of their far leg
- When they turn away to escape the leg drag, follow their hip movement
- Step over their body and begin circling toward their back
- As they continue turning, establish your first hook behind their thigh
- Secure seatbelt grip and work to establish the second hook for full back control

- From truck position (controlling their far leg while they're on their side), maintain your leg control
- Use your free hand to control their upper body and prevent them from turning back toward you
- Roll them forward while following their movement toward their back
- As they roll, immediately work to establish your first hook
- Secure seatbelt grip and establish the second hook for full back control

- From X guard, maintain your X hook structure while controlling their upper body
- Elevate them with your X guard and sweep them forward over your head
- As they roll over you, immediately follow their movement and start climbing up their back
- Establish your first hook as they land in front of you
- Secure seatbelt control and work to establish the second hook for back control

- From De La Riva guard, establish a strong DLR hook and control their opposite collar or sleeve
- Invert underneath them by rolling backward and to the side of your DLR hook
- Use your free leg to hook around their far hip as you continue the berimbolo roll
- Come up behind them as they're forced to turn, immediately establishing your first hook
- Secure seatbelt grip and work to establish the second hook for full back control

- From reverse De La Riva passing position, maintain control of their legs while staying mobile
- When they turn away to defend or reguard, follow their hip movement
- Circle around their legs toward their back, maintaining leg control to prevent reguarding
- As you move behind them, release leg control and establish your first hook
- Secure seatbelt grip and work to establish the second hook for back control

- From bottom half guard, secure an underhook on their far side arm and control their wrist with your other hand
- Apply kimura grip by threading your underhook hand through and grabbing your own wrist
- Use the kimura control to roll them over your trapped leg while maintaining the grip
- As they roll, release your trapped leg and immediately work to get your hooks in for back control
- Secure the back mount position while maintaining kimura control for additional submission threats

- From De La Riva guard, maintain your hook behind their knee and collar grip
- Duck under their leg while maintaining your De La Riva hook and drive forward
- Roll through in a somersault motion, keeping your hook engaged throughout the roll
- As you complete the roll, your opponent should be pulled over you and land on their side
- Immediately secure back control by getting your hooks in and establishing a seatbelt grip

- From octopus guard with your leg wrapped around their arm and controlling their opposite sleeve
- Use your wrapped leg to pull their arm across their body while sitting up
- Duck under their extended arm and circle behind them
- Secure back control by getting your hooks in and establishing seatbelt grip
- Maintain control of their far arm to prevent them from turning back into you

- From top half guard, secure an underhook on their far side and control their near side arm
- Drive your weight forward and initiate a forward roll over their body
- Maintain your grips throughout the roll while keeping your trapped leg engaged
- As you complete the roll, your opponent should end up on top but facing away from you
- Immediately secure your hooks and establish back control with a seatbelt grip

- From reverse side control (facing their legs), secure a grip on their far hip and control their near leg
- Step your outside leg over their body and begin to roll backwards
- Use your grips to pull them with you as you execute the backward roll
- Complete the roll so they land on their stomach with you on their back
- Secure your hooks and establish back control with proper hand positioning

- When caught in an americana from side control or mount, immediately grab your own wrist being attacked
- Pull your elbow toward your ribs while keeping your forearm close to your body
- Use your free hand to push against their grip or forearm to create space
- Once you create enough space, slip your elbow out of their control
- Immediately frame and work to improve your position or continue escaping

- When caught in an americana, grab your attacked wrist with your free hand for support
- Push your elbow away from your body and toward their grip to create counter-pressure
- Use your body weight and core strength to drive your elbow in the opposite direction of their leverage
- As their grip loosens, quickly pull your arm free and establish frames
- Immediately work to improve your position or continue your escape sequence

- When caught in an americana from side control or mount, keep your attacked arm close to your body
- Turn your entire body toward the side of your trapped arm while keeping your elbow tight
- Use your free hand to push against their hip or body to assist the turn
- As you turn to your side, your shoulder alignment changes and reduces their leverage
- Complete the turn to face them and work to recover guard or improve position

subcategory: Ankle Lock Escape (Put on the Boot)
description:
- When caught in ashi garami with an ankle lock, immediately grab your own shin/foot ("put on the boot")
- Pull your foot toward your glutes while keeping your knee pointing up
- Use your free hand to control their grip or push against their arms
- Turn your knee inward to reduce the angle of attack on your ankle
- Work to extract your foot while maintaining the protective "boot" grip until you're clear

- When your arm is being attacked from mount, immediately drive your elbow to the mat on the side they're attacking
- Keep your elbow glued to the ground and turn your thumb toward the mat
- Use your free hand to push against their hip or leg to prevent them from adjusting
- Maintain the elbow connection to the mat while working to turn your body
- Once you create enough angle, work to extract your arm and recover guard

- As they attempt the armbar from mount, immediately turn toward them and drive your head to the inside of their thigh
- Keep your attacked arm bent and close to your body while driving forward with your head
- Use your free hand to control their leg or hip to prevent them from adjusting
- Continue driving your head deeper between their legs to reduce their leverage
- Work to stack them or turn to extract your arm once you've compromised their position

- From mount when opponent attempts armbar, keep your trapped arm bent and close to your body
- As they swing their leg over, immediately turn toward your trapped arm side
- Use your free hand to grab their ankle or shin that's across your face
- Lift their leg up and over your head while continuing to turn, creating space
- Pull your arm out and establish side control or guard recovery

- When caught in armbar from guard, immediately clasp your hands together
- Stack your opponent by driving your weight forward and standing up on your toes
- Keep your head low and drive your shoulder into their hips
- Once stacked, perform the bulldog by grabbing their belt or pants
- Lift and drive them over their head while maintaining your grip, then pass to side control

- From back control, identify which hook is deeper and address it first
- Grab the ankle of the deeper hook with your same-side hand
- Drive your hip down and away from that hook while pulling the ankle
- Once first hook is removed, immediately address the second hook
- Turn toward the side you cleared and work to establish guard or stand up

- From back control, keep your arms straight and elbows tight to your ribs
- Grab your opponent's wrists or sleeves to prevent choking attempts
- Scoot your hips down toward their knees to create distance from their arms
- Turn your head to one side and drive that shoulder down
- Continue turning until you can face your opponent and establish guard

- From back control with body triangle, identify the top leg of their triangle
- Insert your knee between your body and their top leg
- Use your knee to create a wedge and pump it deeper
- Grab their ankle and push their leg down while lifting your knee up
- Once the triangle breaks, turn to face them and establish guard

- From back control with body triangle, post your hands on the ground
- Come up to your knees while keeping your back straight
- Stand up explosively, lifting your opponent's weight
- Once standing, bend forward and grab their ankles or lower legs
- Drive forward to break the body triangle and dump them forward

- From back control with body triangle, identify their bottom leg
- Reach down and grab their bottom ankle with your same-side hand
- Trap their leg by hooking it with your leg on the same side
- Use your grip and leg trap to pry their triangle apart
- Once broken, turn to face them and work to establish guard or stand

- When opponent grips your collar for a choke, immediately grab their choking hand
- Use both hands to grip their wrist and pull it away from your neck
- Keep your chin down and shoulders hunched to protect your neck
- Break their grip by twisting their wrist or using a two-on-one grip break
- Once grip is broken, control their arms and work your escape or counter

- When opponent has collar choke grip, grab their choking arm with both hands
- Instead of breaking the grip, use their arm to pull yourself closer
- Slide your arm under their armpit and around their back
- Establish your own collar choke grip with your free hand
- Apply your choke while using their grip to maintain close distance

- From leg entanglement when heel hook is applied, immediately grab your trapped foot
- Turn your knee toward the ground (internally rotate your hip)
- Get up to a sprinter's stance with your free leg forward
- Drive forward explosively while maintaining internal rotation of trapped leg
- Pull your foot free and establish distance or counter-attack

- From leg entanglement with opponent controlling your heel, immediately grab their controlling arm with both hands
- Stand up explosively while maintaining grip on their arm to prevent heel hook finishing
- Drive your trapped leg down and through their legs while standing
- Smash your weight down onto their legs and hips to break the entanglement
- Extract your leg completely and establish a safe distance or dominant position

subcategory: Kimura Escape (Defend Hand, Pass to Back)
description:
- When opponent attempts kimura, immediately grab your own wrist or gi with your free hand
- Keep your elbow tight to your body and resist the shoulder rotation
- Use your free hand to control their head or collar
- Circle your body toward their back while maintaining defensive grip
- Complete the back take by getting your hooks in or establishing back control

subcategory: Knee on Belly Escape (Belt Grab Ankle Pick)
description:
- From bottom of knee on belly, grab opponent's belt or gi at their hip with your far-side hand
- Use your near-side hand to grab their ankle on the knee-on-belly leg
- Pull their belt toward you while simultaneously lifting and pushing their ankle away
- This creates an ankle pick that dumps them to the side
- Follow through by coming up to your knees or establishing top position

subcategory: Knee on Belly Escape (Force Half Guard)
description:
- From bottom of knee on belly, use your near-side arm to underhook their knee-on-belly leg
- Grab their far-side leg with your far-side hand at the knee or thigh
- Pull both legs toward you while bridging your hips up
- Force their knee-on-belly leg between your legs to create half guard
- Secure the half guard by locking your legs around their trapped leg

- From bottom mount, trap opponent's arm by grabbing their wrist and pulling it across your body
- Simultaneously trap their same-side leg by hooking it with your foot
- Bridge explosively toward the trapped side while holding their arm tight
- Roll them over using the momentum from your bridge
- End up in their guard or establish top position

- From bottom mount, bridge up explosively to create space and unbalance opponent
- Immediately grab and hold their arm or collar when they post to catch themselves
- Shrimp your hips out to the side while maintaining the grip
- Continue shrimping until you can get your knee between you and opponent
- Recover to guard or continue escaping to a neutral position

- From bottom mount, bring your elbow and knee together on one side
- Create a tight frame by connecting your elbow to your knee
- Use this frame to prevent opponent from settling their weight
- Shrimp your hips away from the framed side
- Work your knee through the gap to recover guard or escape completely

- From bottom mount, place both hands on opponent's hips or belt
- Explosively bridge up while simultaneously pulling their hips toward your head
- This creates a kipping motion that launches them forward over your head
- As they go over, grab their legs or hips to control the roll
- End up on top in their guard or side control position

- From bottom north-south, create frames with your arms against opponent's hips
- Shrimp your hips out to one side while maintaining the frames
- Work your outside leg around their body toward their back
- Continue shrimping and working your legs until you can get both hooks in
- Establish closed guard or continue working toward a better position

subcategory: North South Escape (Two on One, Turn)
description:
- From bottom north-south, grab opponent's far arm with both hands (two-on-one grip)
- Pull their arm across your body while turning toward that side
- Use your legs to help turn your body toward their trapped arm
- Continue turning until you're facing the same direction as opponent
- Establish back control or work to a more favorable position

- From omoplata position with opponent controlling your shoulder, keep your trapped arm close to your body
- Drive forward and down toward your opponent's hip, diving under their leg
- Use your free hand to post on the mat and create space as you dive through
- Roll through to escape the shoulder lock and come up to a neutral position
- Maintain forward pressure throughout the movement to prevent them from adjusting

- From omoplata position, immediately recognize the shoulder lock threat
- Jump your legs across your opponent's back toward their opposite side
- Use your free hand to post and help propel your body over their back
- Land in side control or mount position on the opposite side
- Keep your trapped arm close to your body during the jump to prevent injury

- From omoplata position, tuck your chin and prepare to roll forward
- Drive your shoulder toward the mat and initiate a forward roll
- Use your free hand to guide the roll and maintain momentum
- Roll completely over your shoulder to escape the lock
- Come up to your knees facing your opponent in a neutral position

subcategory: Scarf Hold Escape (Legs Up to Armbar)
description:
- From bottom of scarf hold, bring your legs up toward your opponent's head
- Hook your leg over their far arm (the one not controlling your head)
- Use your legs to pull their arm across your body while bridging
- Secure their wrist with both hands and extend your hips for the armbar
- Keep your knees tight together and arch your back to finish the submission

- From bottom side control, frame against their hip and shoulder with your arms
- Bridge explosively while turning toward your opponent
- As they post to prevent the roll, quickly shrimp your hips away
- Insert your knee between you and your opponent to create guard
- Use your frames to maintain distance and complete the reguard

- From bottom side control, create space by framing against their hip
- Sit up and wrap both arms around their legs in a double leg position
- Drive forward with your shoulder into their thighs while lifting
- Take them down and pass to top position or secure takedown points
- Keep your head to the outside of their legs to avoid guillotines

- From bottom side control, frame against their hip with your bottom arm
- Bridge and shrimp to create space between your bodies
- Insert your knee shield between you and your opponent
- Work your other leg through to establish full guard or half guard
- Use your frames to control distance and prevent them from settling back down

subcategory: Side Control Escape (Scarf Hold Back Take)
description:
- From bottom side control when opponent transitions to scarf hold
- Swim your inside arm under their armpit as they switch positions
- Hook their far arm with your inside arm and control their wrist
- Roll them over your body toward their trapped arm side
- Take their back as they roll, securing hooks and back control

- From bottom side control, create a frame against their hip with your bottom arm
- Shrimp your hips away while turning to face their legs
- Spin underneath them toward their back, staying low to the mat
- Emerge behind them and secure back control with hooks
- Keep your head low during the spin to avoid their crossface attempts

subcategory: Triangle Escape (Feet on Top, Ankle Lock)
description:
- From triangle choke position, immediately posture up and stack your opponent
- Place both feet on top of their thighs or hips for leverage
- Grab their ankle or foot with both hands in an ankle lock grip
- Apply pressure by pulling their foot toward you while pushing with your feet
- This creates a counter-submission that forces them to release the triangle

- From inside a triangle choke, identify which leg is across your neck (the choking leg)
- Grab the knee of the choking leg with both hands and pull it down toward the mat
- Drive your shoulder into their hip on the same side while pulling the knee down
- Create space by pushing their knee to the ground and slip your head out
- Immediately posture up and establish distance to prevent re-engagement

- From inside a triangle, place both hands on their hips and drive forward to stack them
- Keep your posture low and drive your weight through their hips toward their head
- As they adjust or try to re-tighten, grab their choking leg and rotate your body
- Turn your shoulders perpendicular to their body while maintaining the stack pressure
- Continue rotating until you can slip your head free and establish top position

- From turtle position with opponent controlling your back, tuck your chin and prepare to invert
- Roll backward over your shoulder while keeping your knees tight to your chest
- As you invert, use your hands to guide the roll and maintain control of the movement
- Complete the roll by bringing your legs between you and your opponent
- Establish guard position by controlling their arms or collar as you come up

- From turtle with opponent on your back, reach across with your far arm to grab their far leg
- Drive your head and shoulder into their near hip while maintaining the leg grip
- Roll toward the side you're gripping, using your momentum to take them over
- Keep your grip on their leg throughout the roll to prevent them from posting
- Finish on top in side control or continue to mount depending on their reaction

- From turtle position, identify when opponent has one leg extended for base
- Reach back with your near-side hand to grab their extended ankle or foot
- Drive your shoulder into their hip while pulling their leg toward you
- Use your momentum to sweep them over as they lose their base
- Follow through to establish top position, typically ending in side control

- From De La Riva guard with opponent controlling your collar and sleeve
- Step your trapped leg (the one in their De La Riva hook) back and around their body
- Keep your weight low and drive your shoulder into their hip as you circle
- Use your free hand to control their far hip or belt to prevent them from following
- Complete the backstep to establish side control or knee-on-belly position

- From open guard with grips established, identify when opponent commits weight forward
- Step your outside leg back and around their body while maintaining upper body control
- Keep your posture low and drive your shoulder into their hip during the movement
- Use your grips to prevent them from turning to face you as you circle
- Complete the backstep to secure side control or transition to back control

- From shin-on-shin guard with your shin across their shin, control their opposite sleeve
- Remove your shin and step that leg back and around their body
- Keep your weight distributed and drive your shoulder toward their hip
- Use your sleeve grip to prevent them from turning into you during the pass
- Establish side control by securing the underhook and controlling their far hip

- From butterfly guard, secure a body-lock by wrapping both arms around their torso
- Keep your head tight to their chest and maintain strong posture
- Drive forward with your hips while lifting slightly with your butterfly hooks
- As they react, step one leg to the side and drive your weight through their guard
- Settle into side control while maintaining the body-lock grip for control

- From butterfly guard, establish a 2-on-1 grip on one of their arms
- Control their wrist with one hand and their elbow/tricep with the other
- Drive their controlled arm across their body while moving your hips to that side
- Use your butterfly hook on the same side to elevate and off-balance them
- Step around their guard to establish side control while maintaining arm control

- From reverse De La Riva guard, establish grips on their collar and sleeve while they have the reverse DLR hook
- Step your trapped leg back and pivot your hips away from their hook (the "Chubby Checker" twist)
- Use your free leg to backstep around their guard while maintaining upper body control
- Clear their remaining leg and settle into side control or mount
- Keep constant pressure and don't allow them to re-establish guard during the transition

- From spider/lasso guard with your hand trapped by their foot on your bicep, grip their ankle with your free hand
- Step back with the leg opposite to your trapped arm to create space and angle
- Circle your trapped arm in a wide arc away from their body while lifting their foot off your bicep
- Once your arm is free, immediately establish grips and posture to prevent re-engagement
- Drive forward to pass their guard while controlling their legs

- From half guard top position, establish a crossface with your far arm across their face and neck
- Drive your weight into the crossface while keeping your trapped leg heavy
- Work to free your trapped leg by creating space with hip movement and leg positioning
- Once your leg is free, immediately transition your body across theirs toward side control
- Secure the position by establishing proper side control grips and weight distribution

- From De La Riva guard, control their collar and sleeve while they have the DLR hook on your leg
- Step your free leg across their body toward their opposite shoulder (cross knee slide)
- Drive your knee toward the mat while maintaining upper body control
- Clear their DLR hook by pressuring down and sliding your leg free
- Complete the pass by settling into side control with proper weight distribution

- From open guard, establish double underhooks on both of their legs at the knee/thigh level
- Lift their legs up and stack their weight onto their shoulders
- Step to one side while maintaining the underhooks and driving forward
- Keep their legs elevated as you circle around to side control
- Settle your weight down and establish proper side control grips

- From open guard, establish a guillotine grip around their neck when they posture up
- Use the guillotine threat to force them to quarter guard (one leg between yours)
- Maintain the guillotine pressure while stepping your outside leg over their back
- Drive your weight forward and use the guillotine to control their posture
- Transition to mount or side control while keeping the submission threat active

- From spider/lasso guard with their foot on your bicep, slide both hands under their foot
- Grip their ankle or foot with both hands while keeping your elbows tight
- Lift their foot up and away from your bicep while stepping back
- Once their foot is cleared, immediately establish grips and drive forward
- Pass their guard by controlling their legs and advancing to side control

- From closed guard bottom, stand up by posting your hands on their hips and rising to your feet
- Keep your posture tall and break their guard by driving your hips forward
- Control their legs by gripping their pants at the knees or ankles
- Step back and to one side while lifting their legs to create passing angle
- Drive forward around their legs to achieve side control or mount

- From single leg deep half guard, isolate their far arm and secure a kimura grip (figure-four)
- Use the kimura control to prevent their movement and create leverage
- Step your outside leg over their body while maintaining the kimura
- Drive your weight forward and use the kimura to roll them away from you
- Complete the pass by settling into side control while keeping the kimura threat

- From half guard top position, establish an underhook on their far side with your inside arm
- Drive your underhook deep and lift their shoulder off the mat
- Slide your outside knee across their belly toward their far hip
- Free your trapped leg by creating space and sliding it out
- Complete the knee slide by driving through to side control with the underhook maintained

- From de la riva guard, control their collar with your free hand and maintain the de la riva hook
- Step your outside leg wide and drive your knee toward the mat to flatten their leg
- Use your collar grip to pull them forward while pushing their trapped leg across your body
- Circle around their legs to establish side control, keeping their legs pinned to one side

- From open guard, grip their pants at the knee with both hands
- Drive forward and push their knees together while stepping to one side
- Drag their legs across your body to the opposite side of where you're moving
- Keep your chest heavy on their legs as you circle around to establish side control
- Maintain pressure to prevent them from recovering guard

- From half butterfly guard, control their far shoulder with your outside hand
- Thread your inside arm under their butterfly hook leg and grab their far hip
- Lift their butterfly hook while driving your weight forward and down
- Smash their leg to the mat and slide your knee across to establish side control
- Keep your head low and chest heavy to prevent them from recovering

- From de la riva guard, maintain your hook while gripping their collar or sleeve
- Use your free leg to pin their non-hooked leg to the mat
- Drive your weight forward while keeping their leg pinned down
- Circle around the pinned leg to establish side control or knee on belly
- Keep constant pressure on the pinned leg throughout the pass

- From reverse de la riva guard, control their collar and maintain your reverse hook
- Thread your free leg between their legs, weaving it around their trapped leg
- Use your collar grip to pull them forward while your leg weave controls their mobility
- Drive your weight over their legs and circle to the side for the pass
- Establish side control while keeping their legs controlled

- From shin on shin guard, grip their collar and control their same-side sleeve
- Lift their foot off your shin while simultaneously dropping your knee to the mat
- Drive forward with your shoulder into their chest as their leg becomes elevated
- Circle around their raised leg to establish side control
- Keep your head low and maintain forward pressure throughout

- From inside closed guard, break their guard by standing or using knee pressure
- Drop low and drive your shoulder into their sternum while controlling their hips
- Keep your head to one side and walk your knees forward in small steps
- Maintain heavy shoulder pressure as you advance past their legs
- Establish side control once you clear their hip line

- From open guard, grip both their pants at the knees with a strong grip
- Stand up explosively while lifting their legs up and to one side like a matador
- Step around their legs to the opposite side while keeping them elevated
- Drop your weight down to establish side control or knee on belly
- Control their far shoulder to prevent them from turning away

- From inside closed guard, place one knee in their tailbone/lower back area
- Use your hands to control their collar or cross-face while applying knee pressure
- Drive your knee forward to create space and break their guard
- Once open, drive your shoulder into their chest and advance your position
- Keep your knee pressure constant as you work to establish side control

- From open guard, establish an underhook on one side and an overhook on the other
- Drive your underhook shoulder into their chest while lifting with the underhook
- Use your overhook to control their arm and prevent them from framing
- Circle toward your underhook side while maintaining tight connection
- Establish side control or north-south position once you clear their legs

- From spider/lasso guard, identify the lasso leg that's wrapped around your arm
- Use your free hand to pin their lasso leg to the mat while maintaining posture
- Sprawl your legs back to create distance and pressure on their pinned leg
- Keep your weight forward and drive through the pin to flatten their guard
- Circle to the side opposite the pinned leg to complete the pass

- From de la riva guard with their hook behind your leg, grab their collar or shoulder
- Step your hooked leg back and pivot to face them squarely
- Use your grip to pull yourself forward while clearing the de la riva hook
- Keep your base wide and posture strong as you re-establish square positioning
- Control their legs or hips to prevent them from re-entering guard

- From single leg X guard, identify their foot that's hooking behind your knee
- Grab their ankle or foot and pull it away from your leg
- Step your freed leg over their body toward mount position
- Drive your knee across their torso while maintaining control of their leg
- Settle into knee on belly or continue to mount

- From shin on shin guard, secure a kimura grip on their far arm
- Roll toward the trapped arm side while maintaining the kimura grip
- Use the momentum of the roll to break their guard structure
- Land in side control or knee on belly position
- Finish the kimura or transition to other attacks from the dominant position

- From X guard, identify the direction opposite their upper hook
- Drive your hips in that direction while maintaining your grips
- Run your legs out to the side, creating an angle away from their hooks
- Keep your head and shoulders low to avoid their attempts to follow
- Circle to side control or knee on belly once clear of the guard

- From open guard, secure grips on their collar and sleeve or wrist
- Snap their head down toward their knees using your collar grip
- Simultaneously drag their arm across their body with your other grip
- Step to the side opposite the dragged arm while they're off-balance
- Control their back or take side control as they're pulled forward

- From butterfly guard, secure cuff grips on both their wrists
- Stand up while maintaining the cuff grips and controlling their arms
- Pin their knees together with your legs or hip pressure
- Step to one side while keeping their arms controlled and knees pinned
- Drive through to side control, keeping their arms away from their body

- From open guard, grab both their pant legs at the knees or shins
- Stand up and create distance while controlling their legs
- Pin their knees together and to one side of their body
- Step around their legs toward their head, maintaining the pin
- Drive your shoulder into their legs and settle into side control

- From X guard, identify their top foot that's on your hip or thigh
- Trap that foot against your body with your arm or hand
- Sprawl your hips back while maintaining control of the trapped foot
- Drive your weight forward to flatten their guard structure
- Circle to the trapped foot side to complete the pass to side control

- From half butterfly guard, identify their butterfly hook under your leg
- Use your hand to trap their hooking foot against your leg or hip
- Drive your weight forward while controlling the trapped hook
- Step your free leg around to the side for better angle
- Settle into side control or knee on belly while maintaining hook control

- From De La Riva guard, your opponent has their leg hooked with your De La Riva hook
- Use your free hand to grab their ankle or lower leg on the hooked side
- Push their knee outward while maintaining your De La Riva hook to create an angle
- Step your outside leg around their turned knee to start passing
- Drive forward and settle into side control or knee on belly

- From half guard top position, secure a deep underhook on the far side
- Drive your underhook arm deep and lift their shoulder off the mat
- Use your free hand to post on the mat for base
- Helicopter your leg over their body while maintaining the underhook
- Land in side control or north-south position

- From X guard with your opponent's leg controlled between your legs
- Secure a deep underhook on their far side while maintaining X guard hooks
- Drive the underhook deep and lift their shoulder
- Use your X guard hooks to elevate and off-balance them
- Helicopter your body over while maintaining the underhook to pass to side control

- From spider/lasso guard with your opponent controlling your sleeves

- From half guard top position, isolate their far arm by controlling the wrist

- From mount position, isolate one of their arms by controlling the wrist
- Pin their wrist to the mat next to their head
- Slide your arm under their elbow and secure a figure-four grip on your own wrist
- Keep your weight distributed and head low to prevent escapes
- Apply pressure by lifting their elbow while keeping the wrist pinned

- From north-south position with your chest over their head
- Isolate their near arm and control the wrist
- Pin their wrist to the mat beside their body
- Thread your arm under their elbow and secure a figure-four grip

- From scarf hold (kesa gatame) with their head controlled under your arm
- Isolate their far arm and control the wrist
- Pin their wrist to the mat above their head
- Slide your free arm under their elbow and grip your own wrist
- Apply pressure by squeezing and lifting their elbow while keeping the wrist pinned

- From side control, isolate their far arm by controlling the wrist
- Step over their head with your near leg to pin their wrist to the mat
- Slide your arm under their elbow and secure a figure-four grip
- Keep your weight heavy on their chest to prevent movement
- Apply the shoulder lock by lifting their elbow while maintaining wrist control

- From front headlock position with your arm around their neck
- Reach your choking arm deep under their neck and grab your own bicep
- Thread your other arm under their near arm and grab behind their back
- Roll to your side while squeezing your arms together
- Apply pressure by expanding your chest and squeezing to compress their neck and shoulder

- From sprawl position with opponent shooting for takedown, secure an underhook on their far arm
- Thread your underhooking arm deeper under their armpit and around their neck
- Grab your own bicep with your free hand to lock the choke in place
- Roll to your side while squeezing your arms together to tighten the anaconda choke
- Drive your shoulder into their neck while pulling with your arms to finish the submission

- From turtle position behind opponent, secure a deep underhook on their far arm
- Thread your underhooking arm around their neck and grab your own bicep
- Use your free hand to grab behind their head or your own forearm
- Roll to your side away from their underhook while maintaining the grip
- Squeeze your arms together and drive your shoulder into their neck to finish the choke

- From 411/saddle position, control opponent's far leg with your outside leg hook
- Secure their far ankle with both hands, thumbs pointing down
- Keep their heel tight to your ribs and align your forearms with their Achilles tendon
- Arch your back while pulling their toes toward you to apply pressure

- From 411/saddle position, control opponent's inside leg with your leg hooks
- Grip their ankle with both hands, keeping their heel against your ribs
- Position your forearms across their Achilles tendon with thumbs down
- Arch your back and pull their toes toward you while squeezing your arms
- Use your leg hooks to prevent them from rolling or escaping the position

- From inside leg control position, secure opponent's ankle with both hands
- Keep their heel tight against your ribs with thumbs pointing toward their toes
- Use your legs to control their hip and prevent them from turning away
- Arch your back while pulling their foot toward you to hyperextend the ankle
- Maintain tripod base with your free leg for stability and control

- From leg drag position with opponent's leg controlled across your body, secure their ankle
- Grip their ankle with both hands, keeping their heel against your ribs
- Use your body weight to pin their leg while positioning your forearms on their Achilles
- Arch your back and pull their toes toward you to apply the ankle lock
- Control their hip with your leg to prevent them from rolling out

- From outside leg control position, secure opponent's ankle with both hands
- Keep their heel pressed against your ribs with proper grip placement
- Use your outside leg to hook and control their leg while maintaining pressure
- Arch your back and pull their foot toward you to hyperextend the ankle joint
- Keep your head positioned away from their free leg to avoid kicks

- From reap/leg knot position with opponent's leg trapped, isolate their ankle
- Secure their ankle with both hands, heel against your ribs
- Use the reaping leg to control their hip and prevent rotation
- Arch your back while pulling their toes toward you to apply pressure
- Maintain the leg knot configuration to keep them trapped in position

- From single X guard, use your top leg to elevate opponent's leg
- Secure their ankle with both hands while maintaining the X guard structure
- Keep their heel tight against your ribs with proper grip alignment
- Use your bottom leg to control their base and prevent them from stepping out
- Arch your back and pull their foot toward you to finish the ankle lock

- From 411 position, control opponent's inside leg and isolate their foot
- Thread your arm under their leg and grab their toes with a deep grip
- Use your other hand to control their ankle or assist the toe grip
- Pull their toes back toward their shin while controlling their leg with your body
- Apply steady pressure to hyperextend their toes and foot joints

- From 50/50 guard, secure an inside heel hook grip on their far leg
- Thread your outside arm under their near leg and grab your own wrist
- Pull their knee toward your chest while extending your hips forward
- Apply pressure by squeezing your arms together and driving your hips into their leg
- Maintain control of their heel to prevent them from rolling out

- From butterfly ashi position with your inside leg hooking their thigh
- Reach under their leg with your outside arm and secure a grip on your own wrist
- Pull their knee tight to your chest while maintaining the butterfly hook
- Drive your hips forward and squeeze your arms to compress their knee joint
- Keep your head positioned to prevent them from rolling toward you

- From butterfly hook setup, establish your hook behind their thigh
- Thread your outside arm under their leg and grip your own wrist (figure-four)
- Pull their knee toward your chest using the butterfly hook for leverage
- Extend your hips forward while squeezing your arms together
- Maintain pressure on their knee joint by keeping your grip tight and hips engaged

- From standard ashi garami with your leg controlling their leg
- Reach under their trapped leg with your outside arm
- Secure a figure-four grip by grabbing your own wrist
- Pull their knee toward your chest while maintaining the ashi garami control
- Apply pressure by squeezing your arms and driving your hips forward into their leg

- From two feet on belly position, control their far leg with your hands
- Thread one arm under their leg and secure a figure-four grip
- Use your feet on their belly to create distance and leverage
- Pull their knee toward you while pushing with your feet
- Squeeze your arms together to apply pressure to their knee joint

- From Z lock position with your legs controlling their leg in a 'Z' shape
- Reach under their trapped leg with your outside arm
- Secure a figure-four grip on your own wrist
- Use the Z lock leg configuration to prevent their escape
- Apply pressure by pulling their knee toward your chest and squeezing your arms

- From knee on belly, drive your opponent's near arm across their neck with your hand
- Slide your arm under their head and around their neck, trapping their arm
- Transition to side control by dropping your knee and securing the position
- Squeeze your bicep and forearm together while driving your shoulder into their trapped arm
- Apply pressure by expanding your chest and tightening the choke

- From mount, drive your opponent's arm across their neck using your hand
- Slide your arm under their head, wrapping around their neck and trapping their arm
- Transition to side control on the same side as the trapped arm
- Position your shoulder against their trapped arm and squeeze your bicep to their neck
- Finish by driving your weight down and expanding your chest to tighten the choke

- From north south position, identify when their arm is positioned across their neck
- Slide your arm under their head and around their neck, trapping their arm
- Transition to side control while maintaining the arm triangle grip
- Position your shoulder against their trapped arm
- Squeeze your bicep and forearm together while driving your weight down to finish the choke

- From side control, push your opponent's near arm across their neck
- Slide your arm under their head and around their neck, trapping their arm against it
- Maintain side control pressure while securing the grip
- Position your shoulder against their trapped arm and squeeze your bicep to their neck
- Apply pressure by driving your weight down and tightening your grip around their neck

- From 50/50 guard, control your opponent's far side arm at the wrist
- Use your outside leg to hook under their armpit and lift their arm
- Pivot your hips toward their head while maintaining wrist control
- Throw your inside leg over their face and secure the armbar position
- Pinch your knees together and extend your hips to finish the submission

- From back control with hooks in, isolate one of their arms by controlling the wrist
- Remove your top hook and swing that leg over their head
- Keep your bottom hook in for control while transitioning
- Secure their wrist with both hands and fall back to armbar position
- Pinch your knees together and lift your hips to extend their arm

- From closed guard, control their posture by gripping behind their neck
- Overhook one arm and underhook the opposite arm to break their base
- Pivot your hips toward the overhooked arm side
- Swing your leg over their head while controlling their wrist
- Secure the armbar by pinching your knees and extending your hips

- From closed guard with opponent's arm pressed to your far side
- Grip their wrist with your same-side hand and their tricep with your opposite hand
- Open your guard and place your far-side foot on their hip
- Pivot your hips and swing your near-side leg over their head
- Control their wrist with both hands and finish by extending your hips

- From crucifix position with their arm trapped behind their back
- Control their free arm at the wrist with your outside hand
- Slide your inside leg over their head while maintaining wrist control
- Remove your hooks and transition to standard armbar position
- Secure both hands on their wrist and extend your hips to finish

- From half guard top, isolate their far arm by controlling the wrist
- Step your outside leg over their head while maintaining wrist control
- Keep your trapped leg heavy to prevent them from following
- Transition to mount briefly then swing your leg over for the armbar
- Secure their wrist with both hands and finish by extending your hips

- From half guard bottom, secure a kimura grip on their near arm
- Roll them over your head using the kimura grip for momentum
- As you complete the roll, release the kimura and grab their wrist
- Land in armbar position with your legs controlling their head and arm
- Adjust your grip to both hands on their wrist and extend your hips

- From knee on belly, control their far arm at the wrist
- Step your knee-on-belly leg over their head in a 180-degree motion
- Keep your other foot planted for base during the transition
- Sit back and secure their arm between your legs
- Control their wrist with both hands and extend your hips to finish

- From knee on belly, grip their near-side wrist with both hands
- Jump over their body in a 360-degree motion while maintaining wrist control
- Land on the opposite side in armbar position
- Secure their arm between your legs with your thighs pinched together
- Keep both hands on their wrist and extend your hips to apply the submission

- From knee on belly, control their near-side arm at the wrist
- Slide your knee-on-belly leg under their armpit
- Fall back toward their legs while maintaining wrist control
- Secure their arm between your legs in armbar position
- Grip their wrist with both hands and lift your hips to finish the submission

- From mount, isolate their arm by controlling their wrist and pushing it across their body
- Step your leg over their head on the same side as the isolated arm
- Sit back while maintaining control of their wrist, keeping their arm straight
- Pinch your knees together and lift your hips to apply pressure to their elbow joint
- Keep their thumb pointing up and pull their wrist toward your chest to finish

- From omoplata setup with their arm trapped behind their back, control their wrist
- Release the omoplata position and swing your leg over their head
- Maintain grip on their wrist as you transition to armbar position
- Sit back and extend their arm straight, keeping their thumb pointing up
- Squeeze your knees together and lift your hips to apply the armbar

- From open guard, control their wrist with both hands and place your foot on their hip
- Swing your opposite leg high and place it on their shoulder/neck area
- Pull their arm across your body while pivoting on your shoulders
- Clamp your legs together around their arm and shoulder
- Lift your hips and pull their wrist down to hyperextend their elbow

- From side control, isolate their far arm by controlling their wrist
- Step your leg over their head while maintaining wrist control
- Sit back into armbar position, keeping their arm straight
- Pinch your knees together around their arm
- Lift your hips and pull their wrist toward your chest to finish the submission

- From side control, control their near-side arm at the wrist
- Spin 180 degrees toward their legs while maintaining wrist control
- Place your shin across their throat/chest for control
- Extend their arm straight and position it between your legs
- Squeeze your knees together and arch your back to apply the armbar

- From side control, isolate their near-side arm by controlling the wrist
- Step your outside leg over their head toward their far side
- Maintain wrist control as you settle into armbar position
- Keep their arm straight with thumb pointing up
- Squeeze your knees together and lift your hips to hyperextend their elbow

- From standing, jump and wrap your legs around their extended arm
- Fall backward while controlling their wrist with both hands
- Land on your back with their arm trapped between your legs
- Immediately clamp your legs together around their arm
- Arch your back and pull their wrist down to apply the armbar

- From turtle position on top, control their far arm at the wrist
- Step your leg over their head while maintaining wrist control
- Roll them over onto their back as you transition to armbar position
- Keep their arm straight and position it between your legs
- Squeeze your knees together and lift your hips to finish the submission

- From closed guard, control their wrist and bring their arm across your body
- Open your guard and place your foot on their hip for leverage
- Swing your leg over their back and hook under their armpit
- Roll them forward while maintaining control of their trapped arm
- Apply pressure by pulling their arm up and back while driving your leg down

- From knee on belly, control their far arm at the wrist
- Step your free leg over their head toward their far side
- Maintain wrist control as you sit back into the submission
- Hook your leg under their armpit and control their shoulder
- Apply pressure by lifting their arm while driving your leg down into their shoulder

- From mount, control their far arm and thread your near arm under their armpit
- Roll to your side while maintaining the arm control, bringing them with you
- Hook their leg with your free leg and secure the baratoplata grip
- Apply pressure by pulling their arm across your body while pushing with your leg
- Finish by extending their arm and applying shoulder pressure

- From side control, isolate their near arm and thread your arm under their armpit
- Transition to a modified north-south position while maintaining arm control
- Hook their leg with your leg and establish the baratoplata configuration
- Secure the grip by clasping your hands together
- Apply the submission by pulling their arm while pushing with your leg hook

- From closed guard, break their posture and control their collar with both hands
- Establish a baseball grip on their collar (one hand palm up, one palm down)
- Open your guard and place your feet on their hips
- Pull them forward while twisting your grips to tighten the choke
- Finish by squeezing your elbows together and pulling with your collar grips

- From knee on belly, control their far collar with your free hand
- Establish a baseball grip on their collar with both hands
- Maintain knee pressure while setting up the choke grip
- Lean forward and twist your hands to tighten the collar around their neck
- Finish by pulling your hands apart while maintaining downward pressure

- From north-south, isolate their arm and trap it against your body
- Position your forearm across their bicep, creating a fulcrum point
- Secure their wrist with your other hand to prevent escape
- Apply pressure by squeezing your forearm into their bicep while pulling their wrist
- Increase pressure gradually until they tap from the bicep compression

- From side control, isolate their near arm and trap it under your body
- Position your forearm perpendicular across their bicep muscle
- Control their wrist with your free hand to maintain arm position
- Apply the slicer by driving your forearm into their bicep while pulling their wrist
- Maintain side control pressure while finishing the submission

- From side control, transition to their legs and control both ankles
- Step over their body and sit back, pulling their legs with you
- Arch your back while pulling their feet toward your chest
- Apply pressure to their lower back by leaning back and lifting their legs
- Maintain control of both ankles throughout the submission

- From turtle position, control their hips and move to their legs
- Grab both of their ankles and step back to stretch them out
- Sit down while pulling their legs up and back toward you
- Arch your back and lean away to apply pressure to their spine
- Keep their legs elevated and maintain the backward pressure until they tap

- From back control with hooks in, secure a collar grip with your choking hand
- Thread your other arm under their armpit and grab their pants at the knee
- Fall to your side while maintaining both grips and your hooks
- Extend your body like a bow, pulling their collar and leg in opposite directions
- Finish by arching your back and creating maximum extension between the grips

- From turtle position, secure a collar grip and control their far leg
- Roll them to their side while maintaining your grips
- Establish a hook with your leg behind their back for control
- Create the bow and arrow configuration by pulling collar and leg apart
- Apply the choke by extending your body and increasing the distance between your grips

- From a failed guard pass where you're stuck in their half guard or they're recovering, thread your arm under their neck
- Get your forearm across their throat with your hand reaching toward their far shoulder
- Secure the grip by grabbing your own bicep or shoulder with your free hand
- Drive your weight forward and squeeze your arms together while pulling their head toward your chest
- Finish by expanding your chest and tightening the noose around their neck

- From top half guard, thread your underhook arm deeper under their neck toward their far shoulder
- Get your forearm across their throat and grab your own bicep with your free hand
- Free your trapped leg by stepping over or switching to knee on belly
- Drive your weight down and forward while squeezing your arms together
- Finish the choke by pulling their head into your chest and expanding your ribcage

- From side control, slide your near-side arm under their neck toward their far shoulder
- Thread your arm deep so your forearm crosses their throat
- Grab your own bicep with your free hand to secure the grip
- Drive your weight forward and down while squeezing your arms together
- Finish by pulling their head toward your chest and expanding your chest to tighten the choke

- From turtle position with them on bottom, thread your arm under their neck from the side
- Get your forearm across their throat and reach toward their far shoulder
- Secure the grip by grabbing your own bicep with your free hand
- Roll them to their side while maintaining the choke grip
- Finish by squeezing your arms together and pulling their head into your chest

- From bottom half guard, create an underhook on their far arm and get to your side
- Thread your free arm under their neck and grab their far lat or shoulder blade
- Use your underhook to roll them over your body toward the side you're choking

- Finish the choke by squeezing your arms together and pulling their head down

- From bottom side control, create space and get an underhook on their far arm
- Thread your free arm under their neck and grab their far lat or shoulder
- Use the underhook to initiate a roll toward the side you're attacking
- As you roll them over, adjust your grip to get your forearm across their throat
- Complete the choke by squeezing your arms together while controlling their posture

- From truck position with their back exposed, control their far leg with your bottom arm
- Thread your top arm behind their near leg, creating a figure-four grip on their calf
- Drive your forearm into the back of their calf muscle while pulling with your hands
- Apply pressure by squeezing your arms together and driving your weight forward
- Maintain control of their upper body to prevent them from rolling out

- From inside their closed guard, place both hands behind their head and interlace your fingers
- Drive your elbows down into their thighs while pulling their head forward and up
- Keep your posture low and use your body weight to increase the pressure on their neck

- From kesa gatame (scarf hold), slide your far arm under their head and neck
- Grab their far collar or gi material deep with your choking hand
- Step your far leg over their head while maintaining the collar grip
- Sit back and pull their head up into your lap while tightening the collar
- Finish by leaning back and using your legs to control their movement while choking with the collar

- From side control, slide your far arm under their head and grab their far collar deep
- Step your far leg over their head while maintaining the collar grip
- Transition your weight to sit back with their head in your lap
- Use your free hand to grab their near collar or assist the choke
- Finish by leaning back and tightening both collar grips while using your legs to control their body

- From turtle position, control their far arm and step over their back with your outside leg

- Walk your feet around their head like a clock while maintaining collar grip
- Pull up on the collar while driving your weight down to finish the choke

- From closed guard, grip deep in both sides of their collar with opposite hands (right hand to left collar, left hand to right collar)
- Pull your right elbow to the mat while keeping your left hand high

- Push with your foot while pulling with your arms to create crossing pressure on their neck
- Squeeze your elbows together and pull down to finish the choke

- From bottom half guard, underhook their far arm and get to your side
- Reach across and grip deep in their far collar with your free hand
- Use your underhook to roll them over you toward the collar grip side

- From top half guard, swim your inside arm under their far armpit for an underhook

- Drive your weight forward and slide your knee up toward their armpit
- Grip their near collar with your underhook hand to establish the cross grip
- Pull your hands in opposite directions while maintaining forward pressure to finish

- From mount, grip deep in both sides of their collar with crossed arms
- Keep your elbows tight to their chest and your weight forward
- If they bridge, post with your head and maintain collar grips
- Pull one elbow toward their opposite shoulder while keeping the other tight
- Finish by squeezing both hands together and driving your weight down

- From side control, slide your near arm under their head and grip their far collar
- Reach across with your far hand and grip their near collar deep
- Step over their head with your outside leg to north-south position
- Pull your bottom hand toward their far shoulder while the top hand pulls toward you
- Squeeze your elbows together and drive your weight down to finish the choke

- From front headlock, thread your arm under their near armpit and around their neck
- Grip your own bicep with the threading arm to create the D'arce lock
- Place your other hand on the back of their head for control
- Step to the side and drive your shoulder into their trapped arm
- Squeeze your bicep to your forearm while expanding your chest to finish

- From half guard top, swim your inside arm under their far armpit
- Thread your arm around their neck and grip your own bicep
- Free your trapped leg and step it over to the far side
- Drive your shoulder into their trapped arm while squeezing the choke
- Expand your chest and squeeze your bicep to forearm to finish the submission

- From side control, swim your near arm under their far armpit and around their neck
- Grip your own bicep to lock in the D'arce position
- Step over their head with your outside leg toward north-south
- Drive your shoulder into their trapped arm while maintaining the grip
- Squeeze your bicep to your forearm and expand your chest to finish

- From turtle position, swim your arm under their near armpit and around their neck
- Lock your hands together in D'arce grip (hand to bicep)
- Roll them toward their trapped arm side while maintaining the choke
- Land in side control with the D'arce still locked in
- Squeeze your bicep to forearm while driving your shoulder into their arm to finish

- From bottom half guard, establish an underhook on their far side and get to your side
- Hook their far leg with your top leg, creating a lockdown position
- Drive your knee into their inner thigh while pulling them forward with your underhook
- Reach over their back and grab their near-side wrist or forearm
- Crank their leg by extending your hips and pulling their upper body down, creating pressure on their knee and hip

- From lockdown position in half guard, secure an underhook on their far side
- Hook their far leg with your top leg and lock your feet together
- Drive your knee deep into their inner thigh while maintaining the lockdown
- Reach over their back and control their near-side arm or wrist
- Extend your hips and crank the lockdown while pulling their upper body down to apply pressure to their knee joint

- From 50/50 guard, control their top leg by gripping behind their knee
- Thread your inside arm under their leg and grab their foot or ankle
- Pull their foot across your body while pushing their knee away
- Apply pressure by twisting their foot inward while maintaining control of their leg
- Finish by cranking their ankle and foot in opposite directions

- From half guard with knee shield, control their posting hand to prevent them from basing
- Reach under their leg with your bottom arm and grab their foot
- Use your knee shield to create space and thread your arm deeper
- Pull their foot across your body while controlling their upper body
- Apply the lock by twisting their foot and ankle while maintaining leg control

- From top half guard, control their far hip to prevent them from escaping
- Reach under their trapped leg and grab their foot with your inside hand
- Keep your weight forward to maintain control while isolating their foot
- Pull their foot up and across while applying downward pressure with your body
- Finish by twisting their ankle and applying pressure to the foot and lower leg

- While passing open guard, catch their foot as they try to establish a guard
- Control their leg by gripping behind their knee with your free hand
- Thread your arm under their leg and secure a grip on their foot
- Step to the side to create the proper angle for the submission
- Apply the lock by twisting their foot while maintaining control of their leg

- From reverse de la riva guard, maintain your hook behind their knee
- Use your free hand to grab their foot or ankle
- Pull their foot across your body while keeping the reverse de la riva hook
- Control their upper body to prevent them from posturing up
- Apply pressure by twisting their foot and ankle while maintaining the leg entanglement

- From single leg X guard, maintain your leg positioning around their trapped leg
- Reach up and grab their foot with your outside hand
- Use your inside arm to control their leg behind the knee
- Pull their foot down and across your body while maintaining the X guard structure
- Finish by applying rotational pressure to their ankle and foot

- While standing against their open guard, catch their foot as they attack
- Control their leg by gripping behind their knee with your free hand
- Step to the side to create proper leverage and angle
- Secure their foot with your inside hand and pull it across your body
- Apply the submission by twisting their foot while maintaining standing control

- From X guard position, maintain your leg hooks around their trapped leg
- Reach up with your outside arm and secure a grip on their foot
- Use your inside arm to control their leg behind the knee
- Pull their foot down and across while maintaining the X guard structure
- Apply rotational pressure to their ankle and foot to finish the submission

- From closed guard bottom, break your opponent's posture by pulling them down with your legs
- Slide your right hand inside their gi collar, making a deep grip with your knuckles against their neck
- Thread your left hand under their arm and grab your right wrist or forearm
- Pull your right hand across their neck while squeezing your arms together
- Use your legs to prevent them from posturing up while applying the choke

- From closed guard top, keep your posture low to avoid being swept
- Slide your right hand inside their gi collar, getting a deep grip with knuckles against their neck
- Thread your left hand under their arm and grab your right wrist
- Drive your weight forward while pulling your right hand across their neck
- Keep your elbows tight and squeeze to finish the choke

- From bottom mount, create space by bridging or using frames
- When your opponent leans forward, slide your right hand inside their gi collar
- Get a deep grip with your knuckles against the side of their neck
- Thread your left hand under their arm and grab your right wrist
- Pull your right hand across their neck while squeezing your arms together to finish

- From mount top, establish a high mount position with your knees tight to their ribs
- Slide your right hand inside their gi collar, getting a deep grip with knuckles against their neck
- Thread your left hand under their arm and grab your right wrist or forearm
- Keep your weight heavy on their chest while pulling your right hand across their neck
- Squeeze your arms together and drive your weight forward to finish the choke

- From side control, control their far arm to prevent escape
- Slide your near-side hand inside their gi collar, getting a deep grip with knuckles against their neck
- Thread your far-side hand under their near arm and grab your choking hand's wrist
- Keep your weight heavy on their chest while pulling your choking hand across their neck
- Squeeze your arms together to finish the choke while maintaining side control pressure

- From closed guard, break your opponent's posture and control their head with your hands
- Bring your right leg up and hook your shin across the back of their neck
- Grab your right foot with your left hand and pull it tight against their throat
- Use your left leg to push their head forward into your shin
- Apply pressure by pulling your foot while pushing their head to create the choke

- From mount, establish a high mount position with your opponent's arms controlled
- Slide your right leg up and hook your shin across the back of their neck
- Grab your right foot with your left hand and pull it tight against their throat
- Use your left leg to push their head forward while maintaining mount pressure
- Apply the choke by pulling your foot and pushing their head into your shin

- From rubber guard with your right leg controlling their posture
- Transition your right leg higher and hook your shin behind their neck
- Grab your right foot with your left hand and pull it tight against their throat
- Use your left leg to push their head forward into your shin
- Apply pressure by pulling your foot while using your leg to drive their head into the choke

- From truck position with your opponent's back exposed and legs controlled
- Hook your top leg deep between their legs, targeting their groin area
- Control their upper body with your arms to prevent them from turning
- Apply pressure by driving your leg deeper while stretching their groin
- Maintain the truck position control while gradually increasing the stretch pressure

- From butterfly guard, secure a guillotine grip around their neck with your arm deep under their chin
- Use your butterfly hooks to lift and off-balance them forward
- As they fall forward, roll them over your shoulder while maintaining the guillotine grip
- Land in top position with the guillotine still secured
- Finish the choke by squeezing your arms together and arching your back

- From closed guard, break their posture by pulling their head down with both hands
- Wrap your arm around their neck, placing your forearm across their throat
- Grip your bicep with your opposite hand and place that hand behind their head
- Close your guard tightly and arch your hips up while squeezing your arms together
